assumptions.assumption: Playwright with AI-assisted site analysis can handle the majority of promotional/vendor websites, including JS-heavy, infinite scroll, and paginated sites.
assumptions.risk_if_false: Core website import workflow fails or requires alternate connector strategy.
assumptions.next_action: Stage 3 must design a resilient scraping job architecture; Stage 6 must test representative vendor sites.

assumptions.assumption: Target users value provider independence and owned catalog data.
assumptions.risk_if_false: AI-agnostic architecture adds complexity without market value.
contradictions: Evidence supports centralized product data, not specifically AI-provider independence.
assumptions.next_action: Stage 2 follow-up or post-Stage-3 discovery should interview target users on AI-provider preferences.

assumptions.assumption: Discovery Sessions are accepted as useful review friction compared with auto-import competitors.
assumptions.risk_if_false: Review staging slows onboarding and reduces import conversion.
contradictions: External PIM evidence supports validation workflows but not Source BlendR-specific Discovery Session UX.
assumptions.next_action: Stage 4 must usability-test Discovery Session review speed and bulk actions.

assumptions.assumption: Universal Catalog Items cover products, services, rentals, labor, manufacturing, and installation without forcing partial re-architecture.

assumptions.next_action: Stage 3 should use a base catalog item plus type-specific attributes extension model.

assumptions.assumption: Background workers can keep the UI responsive for expected scrape and AI job durations without a streaming UI.
assumptions.risk_if_false: Users experience long-running imports as stalled or failed.
assumptions.next_action: Stage 3 must define queue, status, retry, resume, and idempotency contracts.

market_validation.summary: General PIM evidence validates a real product-data management problem: central source of truth, reduced manual work, better accuracy, and faster time-to-market. Promo-distributor evidence from commonsku validates an adjacent industry workflow market. Source BlendR-specific demand and willingness-to-pay are not directly validated.

direct_or_adjacent_competitors.name: Akeneo
direct_or_adjacent_competitors.source_blendr_gap_or_opportunity: Source BlendR can focus on vendor-source discovery, Discovery Sessions, AI-provider independence, and smaller workflow breadth.

direct_or_adjacent_competitors.name: Plytix
direct_or_adjacent_competitors.source_blendr_gap_or_opportunity: Plytix validates PIM demand; Source BlendR differentiates by extracting from vendor websites/PDFs into a user-owned catalog before syndication.

direct_or_adjacent_competitors.name: commonsku
direct_or_adjacent_competitors.source_blendr_gap_or_opportunity: Strong adjacent competitor in promo distribution; Source BlendR can avoid order-management breadth and focus on vendor intelligence/catalog ingestion.

competitive_landscape.positioning: Source BlendR is best positioned as vendor intelligence plus catalog ingestion, not as full PIM, ERP, order-management, or promo distributor OS.

user_validation.summary: Target users are plausible based on PIM and promo-distributor competitor positioning. Direct user interviews are still needed to validate friction tolerance and top workflows.

technical_validation.summary: Playwright official docs support the browser automation primitives needed for rendering, navigation, waiting, clicking, and multi-page contexts. This validates technical feasibility at capability level, not reliability against arbitrary vendor websites. AI adapter architecture is internally coherent and should proceed to Stage 3 with stable interface constraints.
stage_3_required_architecture_decisions: Playwright job orchestration, crawl limits, retries, and failure modes
Normalized import schema and validation gate
Universal Catalog Item base model plus type-specific attributes
AI provider interface, adapter lifecycle, capability router, provider health contract
Tenant isolation across database, storage, queue, search, and AI credentials

operational_validation.summary: Background workers are feasible and necessary. Operational readiness depends on explicit job observability, retry/resume, idempotency, and user-visible status.

business_validation.summary: External evidence validates that businesses pay for product-data management and promo workflow platforms. Source BlendR-specific pricing and willingness-to-pay remain unvalidated. Business viability is plausible but below readiness threshold until customer discovery or pricing tests are run.

scalability_analysis.retention_hypothesis: Vendor/document memory and owned catalog data can increase retention, but this is not validated.

critical_unknowns.unknown: Actual Playwright success rate on representative vendor websites.
critical_unknowns.next_action: Stage 6 test suite with target vendor sample.

critical_unknowns.unknown: Willingness to pay and buyer budget owner.
critical_unknowns.next_action: Run customer interviews and pricing tests.

critical_unknowns.unknown: Legal/ToS posture for scraping vendor websites.
critical_unknowns.next_action: Stage 3 policy and Stage 7 legal launch review.

contradictions.description: PIM evidence validates centralized catalog pain but not AI-provider agnosticism as a buyer priority.
contradictions.impact: Differentiation may be weaker than assumed.

contradictions.description: PIM evidence is product-centric while Source BlendR includes services, rentals, labor, manufacturing, and installation.
contradictions.impact: Universal schema may need extension model.
contradictions.resolution_path: Stage 3 architecture should use base item with type-specific attributes.

risk_registry.risk: Vendor-site scraping reliability remains unproven across representative websites.
risk_registry.mitigation: Stage 3 designs resilient crawler/queue; Stage 6 runs representative vendor-site tests.

risk_registry.risk: Multi-tenant isolation and AI credential isolation are security-critical.
risk_registry.mitigation: Stage 3 defines tenant boundaries, storage isolation, and credential handling; Stage 6 security tests.

risk_registry.risk: Willingness to pay is not directly validated.
risk_registry.mitigation: Run customer interviews and pricing tests before launch.
Stage 3 includes robots/ToS policy and manual opt-in controls; legal review before launch.

risk_registry.mitigation: Stage 3 defines job status, retry/resume, idempotency, and operational telemetry.

Run customer interviews and pricing tests before launch.

architecture_guidance: Treat scraping as best-effort, bounded, observable background jobs, not a guaranteed full-site crawler.
Design Universal Catalog Item as base entity plus typed attributes/extensions.
Keep AI provider adapters behind a stable minimal interface and route by capability.
Make deterministic validation the write gate from Discovery Session to catalog.
Enforce tenant isolation across every persistence and background-processing boundary.

stage_decision_brief.recommended_direction: Proceed to Stage 3 architecture with explicit architecture guidance and carried risks. Market and technical validation support the product direction at medium confidence, while willingness-to-pay, legal scraping posture, and real vendor-site reliability remain open validation items.
alternatives_considered: Proceed directly to architecture with open risks carried forward
Revise product assumptions around scraping and AI-provider agnosticism
Block progression until vendor-site testing and customer interviews are complete

Promo-distributor workflow market exists, supported by commonsku positioning and customer proof

Architecture may proceed if Stage 3 treats Playwright reliability, tenant isolation, validation engine, AI adapter contracts, and queue strategy as first-class decisions

Stage 3 must isolate AI providers behind stable adapters and capability routing
